# Peak and lifetime consolidation: preregistered protocol

**Primary result, before full transaction outcomes:** the count of simultaneous peak-pooled graduations that no member reached alone. Zero or near-zero rejects the “consolidation creates runners” claim on this evidence. The secondary diagnostic, reserve-weighted lifetime c below 25%, independently rejects it. Near-zero is fixed as at most 2 of 283 clusters. Missing history is unknown, not a zero; a subset cannot by itself establish a full-cohort rejection unless its bounds do so.

Fixed cohort: 283 multi-member v1-text clusters, 1482 SOL-quoted members. Exclude 743 non-SOL launches and 731 SOL singletons. 35 clusters already have a completed member and contribute no additional graduation; they remain in lifetime c.

Reconstruct the simultaneous sum in chain transaction/instruction order, not the sum of individual peaks. Migration transfers existing reserve and is not a new buyer inflow. Post-migration pool/vault history is required for a lifecycle c comparable with stock. Histories end at the cached per-group stock snapshot, so stock and flow use one horizon.

Primary c weighting: **peak_reserve**. The brief’s pooled gross-inflow ratio and a reserve-weighted mean are different estimands; this choice must be locked before fetching full transactions. All weighting variants and a fixed-stock-leader comparison will be shown; the rejection threshold will not be switched after outcomes.

## Corrections and collection limits

A first signature page is capped at 1,000 entries and is not a total activity census when full. Completion needs pagination to the known creation boundary, and successful transactions must be decoded, not inferred from signature counts. Pool and quote-vault addresses add activity absent from curve-only history.

No pre-window launch-name catalogue exists in the repo. A member’s own curve history cannot identify an earlier sibling token with the same folded text. The true truncated-root count is therefore unmeasured unless an external launch index is supplied; an invented zero is prohibited.

The median copy lag does not establish a hard maximum lag. Observed cluster counts near the window edge will be reported as risk diagnostics, not a certified upper bound on truncation. No backward catalogue extension is authorized in this run.

Collection is cached in consolidation_history.sqlite with raw compressed RPC responses and attempt telemetry. The signature census has a 45-minute budget; the subsequent full-transaction stage has a 60-minute budget, with whole-cluster scheduling by ascending member count then root mint. Coverage, failures, achieved rates and elapsed time will be reported. No outcome-based selection or new semantic labels are permitted.

The census collection budget was extended before full transactions, solely because measured RPC throttling made the original collection budget insufficient. The JSON records the timestamped amendment; decision thresholds and cohort are unchanged.
